newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-FORMER CSKA COACH ENDS DISPUTE BY JOINING TORPEDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FORMER CSKA COACH ENDS DISPUTE BY JOINING TORPEDO.

text.p: Sacked CSKA Moscow coach Alexander Tarkhanov has taken over at city neighbours Torpedo Moscow, resolving an internal dispute at the Russian army side but taking eight of their top players with him.
Officials at both clubs confirmed on Monday Tarkhanov had joined Torpedo almost a month after CSKA sports chief Colonel Alexander Baranovsky dismissed him.
Tarkhanov had initially refused to go, disputing Baranovsky's right to sack him, but finally accepted he was isolated at the club, in which the defence ministry has a large stake.

"Tarkhanov has left the team after realising he would not have any kind of support from the defence ministry," said CSKA spokesman Yuri Zemlyakov, who added Tarkhanov had taken eight players with him to Torpedo.
Torpedo Moscow president Vladimir Pilgui confirmed Tarkhanov had replaced veteran coach Valentin Ivanov, who moves onto the club's board.
Tarkhanov's place at CSKA was taken earlier this month by former Russian national team coach Pavel Sadyrin, prompting Tarkhanov's revolt.
Russian soccer authorities gave CSKA until March 1 to settle the dispute and threatened them with relegation if they had not resolved it before the start of the 1997 season on March 15.
